scope: Read-only control-flow review of the candidate-v3 opROP source and the bounded reader failure context. No raw-output scan, compilation, or model/solver execution was performed for this review.

control_flow.finding: HIRAC1 label 60 reads a line batch, calls LNCOR1, then falls through label 70 to CNVFNV. This is the path where line parameters are corrected before convolution.
At label 70 CNVFNV runs; if IPANEL is zero, control returns to label 60 to read/correct another batch.
At panel completion HIRAC1 calls PANEL. When ISTOP is not 1, it jumps directly back to label 70, so CNVFNV can process the retained line arrays at a subsequent VFT without another RDLIN/LNCOR1 pass.

LNCOR1 computes corrected line strength and SPPSP; the candidate event recording those values is restricted to layer 21 and VFT approximately 662.695395555556. Earlier corrections at other VFT values are not captured by that target-only event.
CNVFNV consumes the retained SP/SPPSP arrays, derives line support indices, and records phase-3 candidate events at the selected target VFT.

failure_context.interpretation: The absent prior target-VFT reason-9 row does not prove there was no earlier LNCOR1 correction. The control-flow route PANEL -> label 70 -> CNVFNV allows a retained line correction from a previous VFT to contribute to this target-VFT phase-3 event.

limitations: This confirms a source-permitted mechanism, not the ancestry of the particular buffered line at the phase-3 observation.
The bounded reader receipt read one line and did not reconstruct the complete event history, RDLIN batches, or PANEL transitions.
A missing target-filtered phase-2 reason-9 event cannot be interpreted as evidence that the candidate line never passed LNCOR1; its correction may have occurred at another VFT.
This finding does not establish that the negative optical-depth contribution is valid or invalid, and does not change the preserved numerical failure.
